title: Coptic Calendar
intro: The Coptic calendar is used by Egypt's Coptic Christian tradition and agricultural dating.
summary: A regular Alexandrian year with a short final month.
epoch: Year 1 of the Anno Martyrum (A.M.) era begins in AD 284, associated with the reign of Diocletian. The New Year is called Nayrouz.
year_rule: Months 1–12 contain 30 days each. Month 13, Nasie, has five days ordinarily and six in the Alexandrian four-year leap cycle.
after_note: After day 30 of Mesori, Nasie completes the year; after its final day, the new year starts at Thout 1.
history: The calendar developed from the Alexandrian reform of the older Egyptian civil year. It remains important in Coptic Orthodox life; its Era of the Martyrs is distinct from the Common Era.
limits: This is the Coptic/Alexandrian arithmetic model, not ancient Egyptian regnal chronology. Month names vary by transliteration; Julian/Gregorian correspondences shift.
comparison_bottom: NASIE  /  LEAP YEAR ADDS ONE DAY
